positions.commentary: Investors did not initially identify Uber as a $100 billion opportunity, but it became one.
Tesla is described as having a market cap larger than huge car companies despite having nowhere near their sales.

thesis: This episode argues that transformative technology companies like Uber and Tesla have created massive market opportunities that traditional investors initially failed to recognize, with Uber evolving into a $100 billion opportunity and Tesla achieving a market cap larger than established automakers despite significantly lower sales.

claims.claim: Uber is cited as a transformative technology company that opened up new doors for society.
claims.quote: When Uber trained society, you can press a button on your iPhone and something will happen offline, that opens up every other door to somebody pressing a button and something happening offline.

claims.claim: Tesla is described as having a market cap larger than huge car companies despite having nowhere near their sales.
claims.quote: Tesla has nowhere near the sales, but is a bigger market cap than the huge car companies.

claims.claim: Investors did not initially identify Uber as a $100 billion opportunity, but it became one.
claims.quote: I think when everybody invested in Uber, nobody said, like, this is this $100 billion opportunity.

numbers.what: the number of companies Facebook, Google, Twitter bought annually in 2008-2010
numbers.quote: Facebook and Google are not buying 50 different cute startups a year, like they were in sort of two thousand, eight, nine, and ten.

numbers.what: the number of years Patrick O'Shaughnessy has been doing the job
numbers.quote: When I started, I was told, you know, just stick with it for 10 years. And in 10 years, you'll see a cycle play out.

numbers.what: the number of companies in a single fund
numbers.quote: So 30 to 40 a year, that's a lot of companies in a single fund.
